title: TerraPulse Uttarakhand V2 Synthetic Feature Dataset
notice: River and weather variables are synthetic prototype values created for software demonstration and model-integration testing. They are not CWC/IMD observations.
disclaimer: Do NOT use synthetic data to claim real-world accuracy or scientific validation. These values are designed strictly for prototype pipeline and UI dashboard integration testing.

formulas_and_logic.slope_risk: Derived strictly from mean_slope using geomorphological thresholds: LOW (<10 deg), MODERATE (10-20 deg), HIGH (20-28 deg), VERY_HIGH (>=28 deg). No other variables or labels used.
formulas_and_logic.river_danger_level_m: Stable benchmark assigned per district primary gauge station (e.g. Haridwar 10.0m, Pauri Garhwal 9.8m, Chamoli 9.5m, Almora 6.5m). Does not vary over time or depend on labels.
formulas_and_logic.river_water_level_m: Hydrologically simulated stage height using district baseflow W_base, autoregressive recession k=0.82 (Wt_recess = W_base + 0.82*(W_prev - W_base)), overland runoff driven by rainfall_1d scaled by soil moisture saturation factor (0.5 + 1.5*soil_moisture) and slope factor (0.85 + 0.005*mean_slope), sub-surface baseflow contribution from (rainfall_3d - rainfall_1d), and small Gaussian sensor noise (sigma=0.025m). Clamped to min 0.75*W_base. Uses only backward/current info, zero target leakage.
formulas_and_logic.river_level_ratio_to_danger: river_water_level_m / river_danger_level_m, rounded to 4 decimal places.
formulas_and_logic.river_level_change_24h_m: Backward 24h change W(t) - W(t-1) for each district chronologically (0.0 for initial step).
formulas_and_logic.river_level_change_6h_m: Backward 6h change. During rising limb (diff_24h > 0), flash storm surge concentrates 65-85% of rise in 6h: diff_24h * (0.65 + 0.20 * min(1.0, rainfall_1d/50.0)). During recession (diff_24h <= 0), smooth decay: diff_24h * (6/24).
formulas_and_logic.river_level_change_3h_m: Backward 3h change. During rising limb (diff_24h > 0), flash storm surge concentrates 35-50% of rise in 3h: diff_24h * (0.35 + 0.15 * min(1.0, rainfall_1d/50.0)). During recession (diff_24h <= 0), smooth decay: diff_24h * (3/24).
formulas_and_logic.river_rise_rate_m_per_hr: Short-term rate of rise over the active surge window: max(0.0, river_level_change_3h_m / 3.0). Strictly 0.0 during falling or stable river conditions.
formulas_and_logic.temperature_c: Derived from day-of-year seasonal sinusoid (summer high ~June, winter low ~January), elevation lapse rate of -6.0 deg C per 1000m elevation, evaporative cooling penalty from rainfall_1d (-3.5 deg C max), and Gaussian variance (sigma=1.2 deg C).
formulas_and_logic.relative_humidity_pct: Derived from day-of-year seasonal monsoon cycle (lowest in April ~35-45%, peak in July-August ~75-85%), positive modulation from soil_moisture, rainfall_1d saturation (+25% max), Gaussian variance (sigma=2.5%), clipped to [20.0%, 99.0%].
formulas_and_logic.wind_speed_kmh: Baseline terrain wind (8.0 km/h + 0.0015*elevation + 0.15*slope) plus convective thunderstorm gust enhancement up to +27 km/h from rainfall_1d, Gaussian variance (sigma=2.0 km/h), clipped to [2.0, 75.0] km/h.
formulas_and_logic.atmospheric_pressure_hpa: Barometric hypsometric equation based on mean_elevation (P = 1013.25 * (1 - 2.25577e-5 * elev)^5.25588), storm depression (-6 hPa max during heavy rain), seasonal barometric wave, and Gaussian variance (sigma=1.5 hPa).
formulas_and_logic.weather_condition: Standard meteorological classification based on rainfall intensity, humidity, and wind speed: Thunderstorm (rain >= 65mm or rain >= 35mm with wind >= 28km/h), Heavy Rain (rain >= 35mm), Moderate Rain (rain >= 7.5mm), Light Rain (rain > 0.1mm), Overcast (rain <= 0.1mm & RH >= 80%), Partly Cloudy (rain <= 0.1mm & RH >= 60%), Clear (rain <= 0.1mm & RH < 60%).

leakage_safeguards: flood_label was strictly excluded from all feature generation functions.
All time series calculations are backward-looking (t and t-1 only). No forward windows, centering, or future data were accessed.
River danger levels and baseflow levels are fixed station constants, completely independent of target occurrences.
Slope risk is derived exclusively from static mean_slope.
limitations: River levels and weather variables are synthetic prototype values and NOT actual CWC/IMD station recordings.
Models trained on this dataset must be treated as prototype/demonstration models and not deployed for real-world operational disaster warning without calibration against verified telemetry.
Sub-daily features (3h and 6h changes) are downscaled from daily storm dynamics using hydrological concentration models rather than sub-hourly logger readings.
